 Oral Judgment

1. Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the order dated 30/09/2011 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First HC-NIC Page 1 of 4 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:30:52 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/596/2011 JUDGMENT Class, Savli in Criminal Case No.627 of 1995 by which the learned trial court has discharged the accused persons solely on the ground that though sufficient opportunities have been given, the prosecution has failed to serve the summons/warrant upon the accused persons.
2.
It is required to be noted that the original accused Shri Yash Foods and its partners were charged for the offence under the relevant provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

3. It appears that though the prosecution has tried to get the address/fresh address of the accused,
the prosecution could not get the fresh address and the summons which were sent at the address which was known to the prosecution were not served upon the accused.

Therefore, on the ground that though sufficient opportunities have been given to the prosecution, the prosecution has failed to served the summons/warrant, the learned trial court, by impugned order, discharged the accused persons for the offences for which they were tried.
4. It appears that respondent nos.2 and 3 who are one of the partners and partnership firm respectively are served.
Though served, nobody appears for respondent nos.2 and 3.
From the endorsement/bailiff report, it appears that respondent nos.2 and 3 are served and service of notice is signed by original accused no.2 Pratimaben R. Shah.
She has accepted the notice on behalf of herself and partnership firm.
In the bailiff report, fresh address of the original accused nos.2 and 3 is also mentioned as 305, Aakashdeep Apartment, Aanandnagar Road, Karelibaug, Vadodara.
Therefore, one HC-NIC Page 2 of 4 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:30:52 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/596/2011 JUDGMENT
more opportunity is given to the prosecution to serve original accused more particularly respondent nos.2 and 3 at the aforesaid new address.
It is reported that so far as original accused no.1 who is one of the partner of the partnership firm is concerned, he has settled in abroad.
His address is Bhaskarbhai M. Shah, 26543, Delrosa, Drive Hemet, California - 92544.
Therefore, even the prosecution may be given an opportunity to serve the original accused no.1 at the aforesaid address.
In case the other accused being accused nos.2 and 3 are still in India and their fresh address is as mentioned hereinabove
, the prosecution against them can be continued.
5. In view of the above, present revision application succeeds.

Impugned order dated 30/09/2011 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Savli in Criminal Case No.627 of 1995 discharging the accused persons without trial is hereby quashed and set aside.
6.
The matter is remitted to the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Savli, to proceed further with the Criminal Case No.627 of 1995.
Original accused nos.1, 2 and 3 be served with the summons/warrant at the above new fresh address.

7. Even if the original accused no.1 is not served, in that case also as the partnership firm and one of the partner are already on record and if the summons/warrant are served upon them, the trial can be proceeded against them.
